audits.title: An audit of high-dose and combination antipsychotic prescribing across the general adult inpatient wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: Trust recommendations for high-dose antipsychotic therapy (clozapine considered; baseline and post-increase ECG, BMI, BP, pulse, bloods)
audits.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 21 on combination therapy, 11 on HDAT; clozapine considered in 9 of 11 HDAT; ECG before HDAT 100% but after dose increase 36%; BMI 100%; BP and pulse 91%; HbA1c 91%; prolactin 46%

audits.other_findings: HDAT prevalence 9% against 28% in the 2012 POMH audit.
audits.citation: Hyland D, Hemmings B, Elagamy Y. An audit of high-dose and combination antipsychotic prescribing across the general adult inpatient wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S82-S83. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.257.

audits.title: Audit on High Dose Antipsychotic Treatment (HDAT) Monitoring at Rampton Hospital
audits.standard: HDAT monitoring guidelines (CSM/MHRA and Royal College of Psychiatrists): bloods, physical observations and ECG after every dose escalation and every 6 months; consent and reasons for HDAT documented

cycle1.result: Quarterly blood and ECG monitoring 8% to 23%; yearly TFTs 88% and prolactin 72%; quarterly physical observations 77% (regular HDAT) and 77% (including PRN).

cycle2.result: Quarterly bloods about 50-60% and quarterly ECG about 40%; yearly TFTs 100% and prolactin 71%; quarterly physical observations 100% (regular HDAT) and 81% (including PRN). Consent forms completed for all; reasons documented in 85% (regular) and 100% (including PRN).

audits.other_findings: 6% of patients received HDAT in 2018. Prescribers were informed of results and a further re-audit was planned for 2021-22.
audits.citation: Das A, Yanson I. Audit on High Dose Antipsychotic Treatment (HDAT) Monitoring at Rampton Hospital. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S182-S183. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.494.

audits.title: Audit of high dose antipsychotics (HDA) prescribing on high dependency unit (HDU) and acute ward, Nepean Mental Health Centre, Nepean Blue Mountains Local Health District, Sydney, Australia
audits.standard: TGA and Medsafe product information and Therapeutic Guidelines maximum doses: 100% of individual and combined antipsychotic doses within limits
audits.setting: High dependency unit and acute ward, Nepean Mental Health Centre, Sydney

cycle1.result: 13/30 (43.3%) above 100% cumulative maximum; 3 (10%) above maximum for regular antipsychotics; 0/30 for PRN; 18/30 (60%) on 2 antipsychotics, 8/30 (26.6%) on 3, 2/30 (6.6%) on 4

audits.other_findings: Recommended review of routine PRN antipsychotics and a vital sign monitoring protocol.
audits.citation: Jawad A, Mikes-Liu K, Mah C, Roy K. Audit of high dose antipsychotics (HDA) prescribing on high dependency unit (HDU) and acute ward, Nepean Mental Health Centre, Nepean Blue Mountains Local Health District, Sydney, Australia. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S328-S328. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.862.

audits.title: High dose antipsychotic treatment monitoring audit
audits.standard: Trust guidance on HDAT monitoring (HDAT monitoring form plus physical health assessment)
audits.setting: Assertive Outreach Team, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 4 patients on HDAT (117-150% BNF maximum); only one had an HDAT form, which was out of date. 39/52 (75%) had a physical health assessment in the past 12 months.

audits.other_findings: Barriers identified: lack of team awareness of HDAT, no reliable system to flag physical health checks and insufficient equipment.
audits.citation: Scott J, Belda J. High dose antipsychotic treatment monitoring audit. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S348-S348. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.912.

audits.title: Audit of high dose antipsychotic prescribing in the havering community recovery team
audits.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists consensus on high-dose antipsychotics as a time-limited trial with regular review and safety monitoring

cycle1.result: 16 (4.58%) on high-dose antipsychotics; 0/16 had the monitoring form; 12 (75%) had documented review, 4 (25%) none.

audits.intervention: Recommended: staff education, better care plan documentation and wider availability of HDAP monitoring forms with pharmacy.
audits.other_findings: First community audit of this topic in the Trust after yearly inpatient audits following a 2014 CQC inspection.
audits.citation: Umeh C, Ionita S. Audit of high dose antipsychotic prescribing in the havering community recovery team. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S354-S355. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.939.

audits.title: Audit of High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy (HDAT) Prescribing Among Inpatients in East Suffolk
audits.standard: BNF and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines antipsychotic dosage; HDAT monitoring form for each patient on HDAT

cycle1.result: 166 (64.6%) on antipsychotics; 2 (1.2%) discharged on HDAT, of whom one did not have the monitoring form completed.

audits.other_findings: HDAT prescribing was less prevalent than assumed.

audits.title: An Audit of Whether Patients on the General Adult Inpatient Wards and the PICU in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust Who Are Prescribed High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy Are Being Monitored as per Trust Policy
audits.standard: Trust HDAT policy: 13 baseline physical health assessments and cardiovascular assessment before starting HDAT; NICE advice that doses above BNF range are justified and recorded
audits.setting: 16 general adult inpatient wards and PICU, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Baseline assessments completed on 226 (81%) of eligible occasions and not on 54 (19%), excluding 98 refusals; cardiovascular assessment before HDAT in 12/29 (41%).

audits.other_findings: Authors recommend raising ward nursing and medical staff awareness of the Trust HDAT policy.
audits.citation: Hyland D, Singh R, Dainton K. An Audit of Whether Patients on the General Adult Inpatient Wards and the PICU in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust Who Are Prescribed High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy Are Being Monitored as per Trust Policy. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S238-S238. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.580.

audits.title: Adherence to BNF Prescribing Standards and PRN Governance in an Early Intervention in Psychosis Service: TwoCycle Clinical Audit
audits.standard: BNF dose limits, PRN governance (instructions, review, benzodiazepine PRN 4 weeks or less) and HDAT form completion
audits.setting: Early Intervention in Psychosis service, Leicester

cycle1.result: Exceeding BNF maxima 1%; polypharmacy 5.6%; PRN not reviewed 1.9%; PRN instruction missing 1.1%; benzodiazepine PRN over 4 weeks 0.26%; HDAT forms completed 1/378 (0.002%).

cycle2.result: Exceeding BNF maxima 2.9%; polypharmacy 10.4%; PRN not reviewed 1.45%; PRN instruction missing 2.1%; benzodiazepine PRN over 4 weeks 2.70%; HDAT forms 3/482 (0.62%).

audits.other_findings: Most measures worsened; recommends EHR hard-stops, automated benzodiazepine review prompts, a polypharmacy proforma and HDAT training, with a third cycle.
audits.citation: Asi S, Sabtan Y, Chakraborty N, Ahmed M, Elamien D. Adherence to BNF Prescribing Standards and PRN Governance in an Early Intervention in Psychosis Service: TwoCycle Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S280-S280. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11653.

audits.title: High Doses, High Standards: An Audit of Physical Health Monitoring in Patients Who Are Prescribed High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy Following Migration to an Electronic Health Record System
audits.standard: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summary standards for antipsychotic monitoring (revised January 2026); target 100%
audits.setting: Community Mental Health Team, Northern Health and Social Care Trust, Antrim

cycle1.result: Monitoring compliance 26%. FYI flag on chart 21%; HDAT therapy plan in place 26%.

audits.intervention: Epic EHR 'FYI Flag' for HDAT and active HDAT 'Therapy Plan' generating investigation orders and appointments for every patient

cycle2.result: Monitoring compliance 58%. FYI flag 100%; therapy plans 100%. All patients with incomplete monitoring had an appointment scheduled.

audits.other_findings: Most common reason for incomplete monitoring was investigations outside the timeframe; prolactin and ECG most often omitted. Ongoing PDSA cycles planned.
audits.citation: Kerr C, Ford H. High Doses, High Standards: An Audit of Physical Health Monitoring in Patients Who Are Prescribed High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy Following Migration to an Electronic Health Record System. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S311-S311. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11681.

audits.title: High-Dose Antipsychotic Therapy Monitoring in a Community Rehabilitation Cohort: A Cross-Sectional Audit From Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: SPFT HDAT physical health monitoring policy and RCPsych consensus statement on HDAT monitoring
audits.setting: East Sussex Rehabilitation Pathway community rehabilitation team, Eastbourne, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Blood tests and weight/physical observations 45%; ECG 27%; GASS offered 27%; HDAT documentation fully up to date 36%.

audits.intervention: Findings presented to the MDT and an action plan formulated; re-audit planned in six months.
audits.other_findings: HDAT affected about 18% of the caseload; 73% were on two antipsychotics and 27% on three.
audits.citation: Eltayeb H, Ahmad B. High-Dose Antipsychotic Therapy Monitoring in a Community Rehabilitation Cohort: A Cross-Sectional Audit From Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S291-S291. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11724.

audits.title: Improving Adherence to High-Dose Antipsychotic Therapy Guidelines in a Community Mental Health Team: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.standard: PCFT HDAT initiation and monitoring guidelines across 8 domains; 100% compliance required
audits.setting: General adult community mental health team, Pennine Care Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Average compliance 60.6% across all domains; HDAT form completion 0%; consultant initiation 83%; 2.13% of patients on HDAT.

audits.intervention: Local HDAT register created with biannual review by resident doctors.

cycle2.result: Average compliance 77%; compliance rose in 5 domains with 100% in consent, annual review, side effects and GP notification; HDAT form 67%; consultant initiation 83%; 2.06% of patients on HDAT.

audits.other_findings: Blood tests and ECG monitoring fell (25.4% and 75.1% relative reductions); HDAT was discontinued in 50% of the baseline cohort after register review.
audits.citation: Prasai S, Olayefelix B, Sajid S, Kelsall P. Improving Adherence to High-Dose Antipsychotic Therapy Guidelines in a Community Mental Health Team: A Closed-Loop Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S338-S338. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11826.
